title: pravapis homoglyph table
description: Latin letters visually identical to a Cyrillic one, and routinely typed inside a Cyrillic word on the wrong keyboard layout (data/chars/homoglyphs.tsv). NORMATIVE for src/pravapis/normalize.py's fold_homoglyphs(): each row is one (latin, cyrillic) pair, folded only inside a letter run that already contains a genuine Cyrillic letter, so a real Latin word is never touched. The reverse direction (Cyrillic -> Latin, for Łacinka input typed on a Belarusian layout) is the same table read backwards, not a second file. The mapping is intentionally not exhaustive and not case-complete: lowercase Latin t/h/k/m/b, for instance, are not close enough to the Cyrillic т/н/к/м/в to fold safely, even though their capitals are.
